overall: The AG found the Chatham Airport Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law. The March 10 notice topic on public comments was sufficiently specific, and the other points were either not violations or not reviewed because they were raised late.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 10 notice topic 'Public Comments/Questions on Chapters 1-4' was too vague to show what the commission would do with the public input.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the March 10 notice was sufficiently detailed with respect to the Public Comments topic where the Commission discussed comments it had received and took questions from the public regarding the first four chapters in the Airport Master Plan Update.

allegations.summary: Raised in connection with the notice complaint: whether the commission was required to let the public speak and whether the notice had to say so.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body provide such opportunity but rather gives discretion to the chair of a public body to determine who may speak or otherwise participate at a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint said commission members made disparaging comments toward members of the public during the March 10 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: An allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility towards the public does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: In the further-review request, complainant alleged a quorum deliberated outside a posted meeting by collaborating on a document later discussed on March 10.
allegations.key_passage: We generally decline to review an allegation that was not included within the original complaint to the Commission because the Commission has not had an opportunity to respond to it.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
